title: Naeem Beg v. Executive Engineer, Electricity Urban Distribution Division-IV, Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Listed; connection abides by final writ; no suit benefit
headnote: Owner's writ against a Permanent Lok Adalat direction to grant a shop connection to the occupant. Prima facie, an indemnity bond under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 may make the owner's consent unnecessary. Notice issued; any connection under the impugned order abides by the writ's final decision and gives the occupant no advantage in the pending ejectment suit.
facts: Naeem Beg claims to own a shop whose earlier electricity connection had been disconnected. The Permanent Lok Adalat directed the licensee to grant a connection to respondent no. 2 without hearing the owner. A civil suit for that occupant's ejectment was already pending and had been disclosed in the Lok Adalat's order. Beg filed this writ. On 5 November 2024 the Allahabad High Court issued notice to respondent no. 2, gave the licensee three weeks for a counter-affidavit, and listed the writ on 13 December 2024.

holding_units.topic: Owner consent where a connection is sought on an indemnity bond, and the interim effect of a connection granted while the writ is pending
holding_units.holding: Prima facie, where the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 allows a connection on an indemnity bond, the property owner's consent is not necessary. The writ was not decided: notice issued to respondent no. 2 and the licensee was allowed three weeks for a counter-affidavit. Any electricity connection granted under the Permanent Lok Adalat's order abides by this Court's final decision, and respondent no. 2 cannot claim any benefit from that connection in the pending ejectment suit.
holding_units.flag: The order names the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and an indemnity bond but cites no clause number. The consent observation is expressly prima facie.

principle_tags.application: Prima facie, once the Supply Code permits a connection on submission of an indemnity bond, consent of the owner is not necessary. The Court did not finally decide the point.
A connection granted under the impugned Lok Adalat order abides by this Court's final decision and confers no benefit on the occupant in the pending ejectment suit.

not_decided.point: Whether the Permanent Lok Adalat could direct an electricity connection to respondent no. 2 without hearing the owner
not_decided.note: Left open. The Court recorded only a prima facie view that an indemnity bond may make the owner's consent unnecessary, and directed that any connection abide by the final decision in the writ.

not_decided.point: The pending civil suit for ejectment of respondent no. 2
not_decided.note: Not decided. The occupant cannot claim any benefit arising out of the electricity connection in that suit.
